title: Kauda and the oil
hookLine: tradition says a man-eating tribesman tried to boil Nanak in oil, and the oil turned cool

cards: Somewhere far from home, the fire is already lit. A great iron pan sits over it, full of oil, and the oil is starting to shimmer. A man named Kauda tends it.

The tellings call him a man-eater, a wild and feared figure of the forest, and he has already seized Mardana. That's where this sakhi opens: not with Nanak preaching, but with Mardana in danger and the oil getting hot.
The road turns frightening. Today: Kauda.

teach.b: In the janamsakhis, Mardana has wandered off, and Kauda catches him. Nanak comes looking, and finds his friend about to be thrown in. Tellings differ on what comes next.

teach.h: THE GURU IN THE PAN, UNHARMED.
teach.b: In the one followed here, Kauda turns on Nanak instead, seizes the Guru and drops him into the pan. And here's the wonder at the heart of it: tradition says the oil went cool. Nanak sits in it unharmed.

Kauda stokes the fire, and still the oil won't burn him. And Kauda, the terror of the forest, stares, and then falls at the Guru's feet. The tellings say he changed his ways and began to remember the Name.
What does this story know? Notice what Nanak doesn't do.
He doesn't fight Kauda, curse him, or call down fire. The heat in the scene is all Kauda's: the fire, the pan, the hunger, the fear he spreads.

And the Guru meets all that heat with a stillness so complete that it cools the oil itself. Read as a wonder, it shows the Guru's protection. Read as a picture, it shows what a calm person does to a burning room.
Either way, the story ends with Kauda changed, not destroyed.

teach.h: THE FIERCE ONE BECOMES A SEEKER.
teach.b: We've seen that shape before on the road: the fiercest person in the story becomes a seeker by the end.
Some readers see in Kauda's oil a picture of what the Guru's word can do to the fire inside a person: cool it, without destroying the person.

how: Sikhs tell the sakhi of Kauda to children and in katha as a story of the Guru's calm and protection, and of a feared man who was changed rather than destroyed.

games.q: Mardana is about to be thrown into the hot oil, and Kauda turns on the Guru instead. in the sakhi, what does the Guru do?
o: fights him with whatever is at hand.
runs for help from the nearest village.
stays still, and lets Kauda do what he means to do.
games.why: tradition says Kauda dropped Nanak into the pan, and the oil went cool. the feared man fell at the Guru's feet and was changed.

practice: Breathe slowly and bring to mind something hot in your life right now, an argument that hasn't ended, a family chat gone sharp, without replaying it; just see the heat.

Then let your breath go slower, and ask what the coolest thing you could bring to it would be: not winning, not silence, maybe a softer first sentence. If you pray, you can say Waheguru as you breathe out.

carryVoice: Your line: the oil went cool. Stillness met the heat, and no one was destroyed. Until tomorrow.
